The supplied units are base-text excerpts of docs/architecture/inference.md (lines 806-1611). The only changed range in file_changes is the documentation table row at line 1846, the `stop` row. The patch scopes GPT-OSS stop-string matching to the Harmony `final` message (`ModelEOSPolicy.stopStringScope`), so analysis and tool-call frames never match a stop sequence, and the reported sequence replays the same scope. The change is documentation only, with no code, config, wire or deployment change. Line 1846 is outside the supplied excerpt text, so I could not read its surrounding source. The excerpt I did read covers GLM5Next admission and step pricing, the calibration and deadline admission mechanics, prompt token cache scoping, and SSD stage ordering. None of it is altered by the patch.

The threat model has T-041 for prefix-cache and TTFT oracle behaviour, T-010 for cancellation, and TB-007 for the inference engine. The described stop-scope behaviour narrows where text matching applies. It touches no encryption, authentication, attestation, key custody or cache-scope derivation, and creates no new exposure path against A-001.

Open question for later passes: the real code change (the Swift sources that implement `stopStringScope`) is outside this batch. Check that stop matching on held-back text cannot cause reasoning or analysis text to leak to the consumer, or tool-call frames to be truncated, in a way that bypasses the reasoning-withholding paths. This documentation excerpt does not establish that. I found no security regression in the supplied evidence.
